answer: Tie grade and vote weight to a slow-built work terrace, not to how many keys an operator can mint. Each identity carries one kernel of attested jobs, and that kernel grows only when randomly assigned reviewers, acting as a falcon watch, sign that a live completion was useful and uncorrelated with known sibling traces. A new key starts with an empty kernel and remains on the bottom terrace. Because each falcon signature is scarce, non-transferable, and void if outputs cluster, a stack of fresh keys cannot be lifted in parallel into voting seats.
